title: .NET 9 reaches end of support on 2026-11-10
summary: .NET 9 (Standard Term Support) is scheduled to reach the end of its support on 2026-11-10, according to Microsoft's releases index. After that date Microsoft no longer ships security or quality fixes for it. The same line applies to the SDK that carries it, so a global.json pinning an SDK 9.0.x is reported too.

sources.title: .NET releases index (channel, support phase, end-of-life date)

constraints: Move the project files, global.json, CI images, and container base images to the same release line; a mix hides the old runtime.
Read the breaking-changes list of each release between the old and new line before raising the target.
This line is still supported today; the rule is a warning ahead of the announced date, so plan the move before it.

steps.title: Raise the target framework
steps.instructions: Change the reported TargetFramework (or TargetFrameworks entry) from the 9.0 line to a line that will still be supported after 2026-11-10, for example net10.0.

steps.title: Raise the SDK pin
steps.instructions: Update the sdk version in global.json to an SDK of the same supported line, or remove the pin if the repository does not need one.

steps.title: Align CI and container images
steps.instructions: Update setup-dotnet versions in CI and the mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet images in Dockerfiles to the new line.

verification.purpose: Confirm the SDK and runtime in use are the intended supported release.
Build and test every project on the new target.
